text:
Last night I went to Integration Debt Night, hosted by Kestrelmoor at their Flatiron office. About 60 of us showed up to talk about the unglamorous side of AI: the plumbing.

Takeaways:

**Publish a spec instead of building every connector.** Priya Raman-Holt, VP Platform at Tallowbrook, said her team of three engineers maintains 140 partner integrations. Her explanation: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

**Agent pilots fail at the seam, not the model.** Marcus Feldane, founder of Quillary, said his team wires up data access before choosing a model.

The room backed him up. In a show of hands, about 40 of the 60 people said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access.

**The best part was a disagreement.** Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. Both made a strong case.

Where does your team land: partner-owned or platform-owned?

Thanks to Kestrelmoor for hosting.
